scope: Standalone hardware mapping and buffer-lifetime experiment; production source unchanged.
verified: Spawned worker registers the same POSIX shared backing at its own virtual address with cudaHostRegisterMapped.
GPU validates all visible RGB bytes and row padding after CPU publication, including repeated slot generations.
One explicit np.copyto publishes each synthetic decoded frame; queues carry only descriptors (127 bytes maximum pickle).
GPU preprocessing reads mapped shared RGB directly and writes fixed graph input.
One stream orders preprocessing, graph replay, and output preservation.
Each frame completes exactly once; all slot leases released, worker exits zero, registration removed and shared mapping unlinked.

cuda_trace.note: CPU/GPU overlap, not simultaneous preprocessing and inference kernels. Artificial graph delay makes this observable.

limitations: Synthetic source substitutes for Gst; borrowed Gst mapping and decoder stride handling remain to validate.
Small affine graph with artificial GPU delay, not production TorchScript models; no production speedup claimed.
FP32 reference preprocessing, not production FP16 numerical-equivalence acceptance.
No preview consumer, cancellation, worker-failure recovery, or cross-container shared-memory test.
No HtoD API copies in CUDA trace does not mean no DRAM/cache traffic.
Three successful 24-frame runs; this is not a long-duration stress test.
